# localmelo

> localmelo is a local personal agent that runs tasks with tools (shell, Python, files, MCP servers) and memory on a model server the user runs (any OpenAI-compatible server, Ollama) or on a cloud API (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, NVIDIA). It offers the `melo` command, which returns a fixed exit code per run and prints one JSON line with `--output-format json`, an experimental Python API, and an HTTP gateway on 127.0.0.1. It is pre-alpha: interfaces may change before v0.1.0.

- Install from a clone named `localmelo` with Python 3.11+: `uv sync --extra gateway`, then run `uv run melo` in the clone (`melo` is not on PATH). MIT license. localmelo never downloads, starts or serves models.
- One task: `melo --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 --chat-model MODEL --output-format json --timeout 300 -- "TASK"`; `--reasoning legacy|drop|replay|compress|compress+replay` (default `legacy`, unchanged) chooses whether a reply's reasoning is sent back, with `--reasoning-field auto|reasoning_content|reasoning` (replay and compress+replay), `--replay-turns N` and `--note-writer auto|heuristic` (compress modes: each reply becomes a RAM-only note and its drafts), `--retriever auto|off|bm25|llm|embedding`, `--recall-at start,attempt,step,tool`, `--recall-k 1..10`, `--recall-kinds note,draft,thought,digest,reflection,long`, `--recall-placement tool|message`, `--recall-min-score 0..1`, `--retrieval-extra-body JSON`, `--admit-on-outcome on|off` and `--keep-decision-text` (R6-lite's typed long store: a candidate is admitted by rehearsal, a user request (which also admits the fact after its marker) or statement, or the outcome switch; one decision per action; `--keep-decision-text` is refused in the UI), and `long_term.db` `user_version` 1 with the typed columns and `decisions` (legacy migrates in place, rows and search unchanged); `melo-retrieve --export-store DIR|FILE`, `--export-decisions DIR|FILE`, `--route CANDIDATES.jsonl --memory-dir DIR` score the store offline (a directory with no store prints zero and exits 0); R5: compress recalls at start/attempt/step by default; auto = embedding if configured, else llm at start/attempt and bm25 at step/tool; tool is never on unless named; a step's recall can include a superseded note or thought chunk of an evicted turn, and `memory_stats.recall_empty` counts a recall that found nothing; legacy refuses these flags); `--workspace DIR` makes the run work in that folder: file tools stay inside it and `shell_exec`/`python_exec` start there (default: the current folder; a path that is not a folder exits 2 with one line); exit 0 completed, 1 crashed or a configuration error, 2 any other status or a usage error. Bare `melo` in a terminal opens the interactive UI (a first run asks for a model server and model and saves them, as `ollama` when the server answers `GET /api/version` like Ollama, else as `vllm`; thinking, tool calls and progress shown live, approvals (with a diff for an overwritten file), `/model`, `/backend`, `/verbose`, `/thinking`, `/expand`, `/progress`, `/approvals`, `/status`, `/mcp`, `/retry`); `--mcp-config FILE` or the config's top-level `mcp_config` loads MCP servers; without a TTY it exits 2. `melo --serve` starts the gateway. Agents: do not run bare `melo` in a pty under the user's HOME, and use direct mode in scripts.
- Worker sessions: direct `--save-session [TITLE] -- TASK` records one turn; `--parent-run ID` needs it. `--import-session dsh-jsonl FILE [--title TITLE]` imports once by content hash. Read via `GET /api/sessions?kind=worker` (filters `status`, `source`, `parent_run`; `cursor` / `next_cursor`) and worker detail/turns; no writes or live follow. Regex redaction is not a guarantee against arbitrary printed secrets; recognizable sensitive file reads are omitted. Thinking follows session retention.
- Saved terminal chats: `melo -c` resumes the newest eligible chat in this workspace; `melo -r [ID|TITLE]`, `/sessions [filter]` and `/resume [id|title]` resolve or pick one. Picker filtering, Tab folder/all-folders and Esc preserve the draft. Startup selection precedes the named banner. Resuming keeps current model/workspace and `/verbose`/`/thinking`, clears grants and explains restored memory (`[sessions] resume_mode = "pairs"` default or `"window"`); `/retry` keeps stored typed text and `/expand` reads persisted tool output. Cross-window changes reload before sending; busy/deleted sessions keep drafts. Only CLI chats with finished turns are offered; no web/scheduler sessions. `-c` and `-r` are mutually exclusive and interactive-only. Direct parsing/output stays unchanged; put task text after `--`.
- Terminal session tools: `/title [text]` shows/sets a title (kept until lazy first-turn creation); idle-only `/undo` forgets the newest finished turn, keeps typed history and never reverses file changes; a committed undo reports success even after Esc, and `/retry` re-runs that undone turn without undoing the previous one. `/usage` includes undone work, leaves missing/running counters unknown and reflows on narrow terminals; `/memory` inspects a copied, cleaned working window and explains the actual resume mode, without model calls or memory writes. `/copy [turn]` copies stored redacted Markdown without thinking, preserving indentation/newlines with bounded turn reads, not wrapped terminal output; local macOS uses bounded `/usr/bin/pbcopy`, SSH/other platforms/failure request OSC 52 (terminal support varies). Tests must fake native copying: temporary HOME does not isolate the OS clipboard.
- Tools run with the user's permissions and no sandbox; `python_exec` code runs in a child process, killed at its time limit. The gateway has no authentication and must stay on 127.0.0.1. Gateway and console sessions offer `file_read`, `file_write` and `python_exec`, not `shell_exec`; direct mode, the interactive UI and the Python API's default `mode="python"` still offer it (`AgentOptions(mode="direct"|"interactive"|"gateway"|"python")`). `direct` and `python` refuse six destructive `shell_exec` command patterns; `interactive` asks its panel instead, and `python` keeps the blocklist with or without a policy.

## Docs

- [localmelo for agents](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/for-agents.md): the one page an agent needs: install, CLI, Python API, HTTP, results, config, tools, memory, gotchas and rules.
- [Quickstart](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/quickstart.md): install, run a first task, save a configuration and start the gateway.
- [Command-line reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/cli.md): `melo` modes, the interactive UI (keys, commands, approvals), every option, output, exit codes and signals.
- [Run results](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/run-results.md): run statuses, the fields of the JSON line and `RunResult`, and retries.
- [Python API](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/python-api.md): `Agent`, `AgentOptions`, `RunResult`, stopping a run, approval policies, permission tiers and the workspace root.
- [Events](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/events.md): the events a Python run reports, their order, fields and rules.
- [Sessions](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/sessions.md): conversations kept in SQLite (experimental Python API): turns, statuses, message ids, resume, approvals for a person and the event stream; `SessionRunner(..., progress=True)` stores a turn's `run.progress`, `run_turn`/`start_turn` take `routine=`, and `build_session_agent` can wrap the providers the Agent is built with (`wrap_llm`/`wrap_embedding`).
- [Gateway and HTTP API](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/gateway.md): HTTP routes, sessions, the loopback guard, the web workspace and the macOS background service.
- [API v2](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/api.md): the web console's `/api` routes (health, settings, key-status, connection test, model listing, sessions, turns, SSE events, blobs, submission lookups, the writes that create a session and start, retry, stop and approve its turns, its scheduler level and typing heartbeat, and the details: tools, grants, memory and runs), the one error shape, the 1 MiB body limit and JSON content-type rule, a runnable create-run-approve script, and the additive-only promise; loopback only.
- [Tools and MCP](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/tools.md): the built-in tools, the MCP config file, permission tiers, which tools each step offers, and what the checks do.
- [Memory](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/memory.md): working memory, history, long-term and procedural memory, and how to keep, inspect and reset them.
- [Configuration](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/configuration.md): the setup wizard, `config.toml`, backends, API keys, timeouts and environment variables.
- [Set up an embedding model](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/embedding.md): long-term memory's embedding backend, the probe that proves one works, and server commands for Ollama, oMLX, vLLM, SGLang and MLC.
- [Troubleshooting](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/troubleshooting.md): error messages and how to fix them.

## Optional

- [How localmelo works](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/how-it-works.md): the run loop, reflection, memory and timeouts.
- [Evaluations](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/evaluations.md): the controlled comparisons behind the defaults, such as the reflection gate (one model, 12 coding exercises).
- [Offline retrieval](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/retrieval.md): `melo-retrieve`, which compares memory retrievers offline; runs do not use it.
- [Procedural memory](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/procedures.md): the steps of recurring tasks, which every run records at its end (`procedures.db` with persistence on) and which `run.progress` events report to a Python caller and `melo` draws as a progress line on a terminal; `localmelo.support.progress_line.format_past` gives that line's past facts and items alone; `melo-procedures` replays the progress rules offline.
- [Scheduler](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/scheduler.md): the scheduling policy core and its simulator, for maintainers; the gateway's web chats and the console's sessions are gated (`[scheduler] policy`, default `off`), and it reads the shared GPU lock and the battery, holding chats while a foreign session holds the lock under `[scheduler] lock_gate = "wait"` (default `record`, which only records); direct runs and the CLI are unchanged.
- [Developer guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/en/developers.html): the repository layout, the development setup, the tests and checks, adding a backend, a built-in tool or a check, and how to send a change.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/localmelo/localmelo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): notable changes; there is no release yet, so all are under Unreleased.
- [Repository](https://github.com/localmelo/localmelo): source code, issues and the contributing guide.
